item: The backup route's Origin/Referer check is the POST middleware's own _foreign_origin, so one function decides what 'this server' means (a proxy's Host NAME:443 with Origin https://NAME is the same server)
summary: GET /api/database/backup refused for itself the requests another site makes (A-008) and compared the sent Origin (else Referer) with the request's Host header as raw strings, while the POST middleware and src/api/cross_site.py's refuse_cross_site_get judge the same headers with _foreign_origin (scheme-default ports normalised, the hostname must be one the app serves, another port is another origin, Origin: null refused). Two functions meant two answers: behind a TLS-terminating proxy that hands the app Host 'oo.lan:443' while the browser sends Origin 'https://oo.lan', the pair is the same server to the middleware and two different strings to the old route compare. NOT observed: the app's own page being refused by it (a same-origin GET carries no Origin, the app sends Referrer-Policy no-referrer, and no file in src/static requests the route); the change is the one-function consistency, not a reproduced user failure. The route now calls _foreign_origin (the Host check and the Sec-Fetch-Site check are unchanged, the 403 text is unchanged, the unused urlsplit import is gone, and a stale docstring clause about the test client's Host name is dropped). One test with the proxy pair in both spellings (Host oo.lan:443 with Origin https://oo.lan, a Referer, and Host oo.lan with Origin http://oo.lan:80) and four foreigners (another host, another port, the other scheme's default port, null); 3 mutants caught (the old raw compare, a hostname-only compare, never foreign), and the file's other 68 tests pass unchanged. Behaviour that CHANGED, stated: behind a proxy that forwards Host 'oo.lan' while the app sees http, Origin 'https://oo.lan' (or a Referer of that form) was served by the old compare and is refused now (port 443 against 80), which is the middleware's existing decision for the same pair; inputs newly accepted are the same server spelled differently (an explicit default port, userinfo, a leading-zero port; measured against the old compare on a twelve-row table), and ftp:// is now refused. The stale sentence in src/api/cross_site.py's docstring ('is to be pointed here later') is RC2's file and is left for them.
